terms.meaning: A short pop-up message that appears briefly and then goes away.
A named style choice, such as default or destructive.
The fixed area on screen where notices appear.

sections.name: File setup, ToastProps (part 1)
sections.title: Notice area and notice box
sections.what: Creates the fixed screen area where notices appear, the notice box with default and red destructive looks, and the provider that tracks active notices.
sections.why: Likely reason: the notice system needs a container and a styled box from the library. Otherwise reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The provider must wrap any screen that shows notices, or none will appear.

sections.name: File setup, ToastProps (part 2)
sections.title: Action, close, title and text parts
sections.what: Creates the parts placed inside a notice: an optional action button, a close X, a bold title and smaller description text. Each has its own styling, with extra red-tone rules for destructive notices.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond composing the notice content.
sections.watch_out: The close button is invisible until hovered or focused, so keyboard users must tab to it.

sections.name: ToastActionElement
sections.title: Notice settings type and exports
sections.what: Defines the type for notice settings and the type for an action element, then exports every part so other files can use them.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Types help other files use these parts correctly.
sections.watch_out: Changing an export name breaks the toaster and the toast hook, which both import these names.

summary: Defines the parts of a small pop-up notice (toast): the screen area, the notice box, its title, text, close button and optional action button.
purpose: Lets the app show short notices that appear and then disappear, for example after a save.
why: Likely reason: the notices are built on the Radix toast library and styled to match the app. Otherwise reason not stated in the code.
how: The viewport is the fixed screen area where notices appear. Toast is one notice box, with a default look and a destructive (red warning) look. Title, description, action and close are parts placed inside it. The variant decides the colors. The close X icon comes from lucide-react.
inputs: Message text and an optional action from the caller, a variant of default or destructive, and standard notice properties.
outputs: Notice boxes on screen. On phones the area sits at the top; on larger screens it sits at the bottom right.
risks: Part of the notice box styling text is cut off in the material available here, so its exact look is not confirmed. Placement depends only on class names.
debug: If no notice appears, check that ToastProvider and ToastViewport are rendered once in the app (see toaster). If a notice is in the wrong place, check the viewport class names. If the close button is invisible, it only fades in on hover or focus.
